cards.b: Oceanic plate subducts under continental plate. Causes powerful earthquakes, explosive composite volcanoes and tsunamis.
Plates move apart and magma rises to form new crust. Gentle shield volcanoes and small earthquakes.
Plates slide past each other. Earthquakes but no volcanoes, e.g. the San Andreas Fault.
Two continental plates push together and crumple into fold mountains. Earthquakes but no volcanoes, e.g. the Himalayas.
A place over a plume of rising magma in the middle of a plate, forming volcanoes, e.g. Hawaii.
A belt around the Pacific Ocean along plate boundaries with about 75% of the world's volcanoes and most earthquakes.
Focus: where the earthquake starts underground. Epicentre: the point on the surface directly above the focus.
Plates stick due to friction, pressure builds, then is released suddenly as seismic waves.
An undersea earthquake or eruption moves the sea floor, displacing water. The wave grows in shallow coastal water.
Composite: steep, explosive, destructive boundaries. Shield: gentle, runny lava, constructive boundaries or hotspots.
A fast-moving cloud of hot gas, ash and rock from a volcano. Very deadly.
A mudflow of volcanic ash and water, often from melting snow or heavy rain.
Measures energy released by an earthquake. Logarithmic: each whole number is about 32 times more energy.
Measures earthquake intensity (effects on people and buildings), from I to XII, using observation.
A scale from 0 to 8 measuring the explosiveness of an eruption by the volume of material and plume height.
Primary: immediate, e.g. collapsed buildings, deaths. Secondary: later, e.g. fires, disease, landslides, homelessness.
Fertile soil, tourism and jobs, geothermal energy and minerals, family ties, and the risk seems low.
Deep flexible foundations, rubber shock absorbers, cross-bracing, strong light materials, and automatic gas shut-off.

gaps.s: When an oceanic plate sinks beneath a continental plate it is called ___.
The point underground where an earthquake starts is the ___.
The Mercalli scale measures earthquake ___ (effects on people and buildings).
The Hawaiian volcanoes formed over a ___.
A fast cloud of hot gas and ash from a volcano is a ___ flow.
Steep-sided volcanoes with explosive eruptions are called ___ volcanoes.
A mudflow of ash and water from a volcano is called a ___.
Fires caused by broken gas pipes after an earthquake are a ___ impact.

short.q: Describe the characteristics of a destructive plate boundary.
short.model: An oceanic plate moves towards a continental plate and is subducted. This causes powerful earthquakes and explosive composite volcanoes.
points: oceanic plate subducted under continental plate

short.q: Explain why Japan experiences many earthquakes.
short.model: Japan is on the Pacific Ring of Fire where several plates meet at destructive boundaries. Pressure builds up as plates stick and is released as earthquakes.
points: located on plate boundaries / Ring of Fire
pressure builds and is released suddenly

short.q: Give two ways that volcanoes can be monitored.
short.model: Seismometers detect small earthquakes before an eruption, and sensors measure gas emissions or ground swelling. Satellites can also track changes.

short.q: Explain why richer countries tend to have fewer deaths from earthquakes.
short.model: They can afford earthquake-proof buildings, emergency services and warning systems, and better healthcare for the injured.

short.q: Explain one short-term and one long-term response to an earthquake.
short.model: Short-term: search and rescue, and emergency food, water and shelter. Long-term: rebuilding homes to stricter building codes and improving hazard planning.
